newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on weak trade.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on weak trade.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices extended midday losses to close lower after producers tried hard to attract buying interest, traders said.
"There was not a single transaction recorded for the day," said an official trade source.
But he added: "This is not surprising given the fact that it's Monday and after a long weekend."
The market was closed from Friday for a religious holiday.
The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted May RSS1 buyer at 284.50 cents ($1.14) a kg, down 3.0 cents from Thursday. May SMR20 buyer was 1.50 cents down at 269 cents a kg.
A check with trading houses showed SMR 20 being offered at 270 cents a kg, SMR CV at 338, SMR L at 317, SMR 5 at 278, SMR 10 at 268 and drum latex FOB at 229.
A trader said on Thursday that prices may fall between 2.5-5.0 cents across the board this week as the market continues to languish from poor demand.

The INRO five-day moving indicator was quoted at 218.46 Malaysian/Singaporean cents per kg on April 17, compared to the 219.43 on April 16. The daily indicator was also lower at 216.18 from 216.83 previously.
